phrases.text: So welcome back again. Time for one more problem.
Now, in this problem,
we are given that
the circular track
is six hundred meter long.
The speed of the first walker is seven meter per second.
The speed of the second walker is five meters per second.
Both start from the same point,
but they move in opposite directions.
The question is asking us to find
after how many seconds they will meet for the first time.
Now, before solving,
let us understand the idea first.
Since they are moving in opposite directions,
they are moving towards each other.
Every second,
the first walker covers seven meter.
The second walker covers five meter.
So together, they reduce the distance between them by twelve meters every second, or simply every second.
Together, they cover twelve meters of the track.
Now, they started from the same point.
To meet again, together, they must complete one full round of the circular track.
One full round is six hundred meter.
Got it?
Perfect.
Now let us solve it.
Since together they cover twelve meters every second, time is equal to total distance divided by relative speed.
Here, the relative speed is equal to seven plus five, which is twelve meters per second.
Putting the values,
time is equal to six hundred
divided by twelve. After simplifying this, we get fifty seconds.
So the two walkers will meet for the first time after fifty seconds. Hence, the correct answer
is option A.
